identity: PowerShell AES/XOR loader carrying Remcos 6.0.0 Pro
reverse_engineering: Outer .bin is ASCII PowerShell. Its first assigned here-string is about 2.2 MB of base64 ciphertext. Static base64 key/IV values and an Aes.Create/CBC/PKCS7 implementation decrypt to a second script, passed to Invoke-Expression.

The second script uses a UTF-8 repeating key to XOR base64-decoded bytes; the result is another base64 string decoding to the FILES managed assembly. It loads the assembly from memory and reflectively invokes FILES.WHORE.LAUNCHER.
A typed decimal byte array holds a native PE. The target is C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework\v4.0.30319\aspnet_compiler.exe. A five-second process-absence loop retries the launch.

Sequencing defect: the wrapper assigns its local payloadBytes after calling the launcher. On the first iteration of the complete outer script, dynamic scope resolves the outer AES ciphertext buffer; when the inner script is considered alone in a clean environment it resolves null. Either value is unsuitable as a PE. The launcher catches failures and retries up to five times; the wrapper then fills the local byte array, which remains available to subsequent loop iterations. This is static control/scope analysis, not observed execution.

Managed IL shows creation of a suspended hidden process (flags 0x08000004), PE header parsing, 32-bit/WOW64 context retrieval, reading the PEB image base, unmapping/reallocating, writing headers/sections, updating PEB and entry context, setting context and resuming the thread. API delegates are resolved dynamically; their signatures and sequence corroborate process hollowing.

The native payload contains Remcos Agent initialized, vendor/family/version banners, remote file upload/download, online/offline keylogger, clipboard, browser logins/cookies clearing, and CMLuaUtil elevation implementation. Existing native RAT, RunPE, downloader and UAC-bypass traits already match.

The SETTINGS resource (type 10) starts with one-byte RC4 key length 210, that many key bytes, and ciphertext. Offline RC4 reconstruction yields 58 delimited configuration fields including the host/port, mutex and filenames, corroborating Remcos. No C2 connection was made.
